review_notes: I read the whole file and compared it with Mathlib. I found no Mathlib or Batteries definition that this file reimplements. It correctly uses Mathlib's Ideal.finite_factors, Ideal.inertia, bot_or_exists_ne_one and Int.quotientSpanNatEquivZMod. The only competing concept is inside the project: Definitions/Def_FrobeniusDensity_BadPrimes.lean (namespace FrobeniusDensity) already defines the same bad-prime set with the same lemmas. This is project-internal, not Mathlib duplication, so it is borderline for this rubric. I did not check whether other P2M files make the same copy, and I did not verify that importing that Definitions file creates no import cycle. I judged the file does not import it directly, and it imports only the Def_FrobeniusDensity_DegOneAsymptotic file that BadPrimes itself imports.

findings.problem: The file defines `towerBadPrimes`, a second copy of the existing `FrobeniusDensity.badPrimes`. The definitions are the same: insert 0, insert 1, then the image of `Nat.card (ℤ ⧸ v.asIdeal.under ℤ)` over the finite set of height-one primes with nontrivial inertia. The supporting lemmas are copies as well. `tower_exists_smul_ne` matches `exists_smul_ne`, `tower_finite_setOf_inertia_ne_bot` matches `finite_setOf_inertia_ne_bot_heightOneSpectrum`, and `tower_inertia_eq_bot_of_notMem` matches `inertia_eq_bot_of_notMem_badPrimes`. The two sets of declarations have the same statements and nearly identical proofs. Keeping both gives two bad-prime sets that are not definitionally linked, so results stated for one do not transfer to the other. The copy also uses `Ideal.finite_factors` where the original uses a hand-written `finite_setOf_dvd`, which makes the copies look different when they are not.
findings.proposed_change: Import Definitions.Def_FrobeniusDensity_BadPrimes. Delete the `tower_*` lemmas and `towerBadPrimes`. Prove `exists_finset_forall_inertia_eq_bot_impl` with `⟨FrobeniusDensity.badPrimes L, fun _ hℓ hB Q hQ hQℓ => by haveI := hQ; haveI := hQℓ; exact FrobeniusDensity.inertia_eq_bot_of_notMem_badPrimes L hℓ hB Q⟩`. If the original's hand-written `finite_setOf_dvd` is the part worth replacing, swap it for Mathlib's `Ideal.finite_factors` there, in one place.
findings.benefit: There is one canonical bad-prime set and one proof of its finiteness and inertia property. The file shrinks to a short wrapper, and a future change to the argument needs only one edit.
